edits.new: aha-htn-2025

edits.match: The current ACC/AHA target is <130/80 mmHg for most adults.
edits.new: The 2025 AHA/ACC target is <130/80 mmHg for all adults with hypertension (additional considerations for institutional care, limited life expectancy, and pregnancy).

edits.match: Annual reassessment of 10-year ASCVD risk informs concurrent statin and aspirin decisions.
edits.new: 10-year total CVD risk is estimated with the AHA PREVENT equations (ages 30–79; replaces Pooled Cohort Equations); in stage 1 hypertension, drug therapy starts at PREVENT ≥7.5% or with clinical CVD, diabetes, or CKD, otherwise after 3–6 months of lifestyle therapy fails to reach <130/80.
PHQ-9, 10-yr CVD risk (PREVENT)
TSH; aldosterone:renin ratio (resistant HTN; consider stage 2 / OSA)

edits.match: 10-year ASCVD risk (Pooled Cohort Equations) — annually
edits.new: **10-year total CVD risk (AHA PREVENT, ages 30–79; replaces Pooled Cohort Equations)** — at diagnosis and periodically. PREVENT ≥7.5% triggers drug therapy in stage 1 HTN; also informs statin decisions (see Hyperlipidemia).

edits.match: Urinalysis with urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) — annually
edits.new: **Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR)** — at diagnosis in every adult with hypertension (Class 1 in 2025; optional in 2017); repeat annually. ACR ≥30 mg/g indicates end-organ involvement.

edits.match: TSH — at diagnosis and as clinically indicated
edits.new: **Plasma aldosterone-to-renin ratio (primary aldosteronism screen)** — all adults with resistant hypertension, regardless of serum K+ (Class 1); consider in stage 2 hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea. Continue most antihypertensives during testing; hold MRAs.

edits.match: Out-of-office BP measurement — confirm diagnosis and titration
edits.new: **Postpartum history of pregnancy-associated hypertension** — BP at least annually.

edits.match: Out-of-office BP measurement — confirm diagnosis and titration
edits.new: **Out-of-office BP (home BP monitoring or ABPM)** — recommended to confirm the office diagnosis and to monitor and titrate therapy as part of an integrated care plan; USPSTF also requires out-of-office confirmation before diagnosis.

edits.match: ACC/AHA (2017) covers post-diagnosis management and surveillance.
edits.new: AHA/ACC (2025; replaced 2017) covers post-diagnosis management and surveillance.

edits.match: BP target disagreement. ACC/AHA (2017) sets <130/80 for most adults.
edits.new: **BP target disagreement.** AHA/ACC (2025) sets <130/80 for all adults, with additional considerations for institutional care, limited life expectancy, and pregnancy. ADA 2026 encourages SBP <120 in high CV/kidney risk and allows <140/90 in older adults in poor health. Per the synthesis rule, the lower target is reflected here; individualize in frail older adults.

edits.match: Pending updates. ACC/AHA hypertension guideline updates are anticipated periodically
edits.new: **Guideline currency.** The 2025 AHA/ACC guideline (Aug 2025) retired the 2017 guideline and is a living document (errata through Jun 2026); verify focused updates at refresh.

edits.match: 10-year ASCVD risk (AHA PREVENT equations) — every 4–6 years for adults 40–75 without ASCVD.
edits.new: **10-year (and 30-year) ASCVD risk (AHA PREVENT-ASCVD)** — adults 30–79 without known ASCVD or subclinical atherosclerosis and LDL-C 70–189 mg/dL; recalculate every 4–6 years. PREVENT replaces Pooled Cohort Equations in the 2026 guideline. Risk strata: <3% low, 3–<5% borderline, 5–<10% intermediate, ≥10% high.

edits.match: Non-HDL cholesterol (calculated) — at each lipid panel; goal approximately 30 mg/dL above the LDL-C goal.
edits.new: **Non-HDL cholesterol (calculated)** — at each lipid panel. 2026 goals: <130 mg/dL borderline/intermediate risk; <100 mg/dL high risk (≈30 mg/dL above the LDL-C goal).

edits.match: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] — once in adulthood as universal measurement
edits.new: **Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]** — at least once in adulthood (Class I in 2026); repeat generally not needed. ≥125 nmol/L (≥50 mg/dL) ≈1.4-fold and ≥250 nmol/L ≥2-fold long-term MI/stroke risk; elevated Lp(a) → intensify LDL-C lowering and risk-factor control.

edits.match: Apolipoprotein B (apoB) — selectively when LDL-C and non-HDL-C goals are met
edits.new: **Apolipoprotein B (apoB)** — when LDL-C and non-HDL-C goals are met, to assess residual risk in CKM syndrome, type 2 diabetes, hypertriglyceridemia, or known ASCVD; elevated apoB may justify LLT intensification even at LDL-C / non-HDL-C goal.

edits.match: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) score — as indicated when 10-year ASCVD risk is 5–<20%
edits.new: **Coronary artery calcium (CAC) score (noncontrast)** — Class 1 (upgraded from 2a) for men ≥40 and women ≥45 with borderline or intermediate PREVENT risk (3–<10%) when the result would change the statin decision. CAC = 0 may support deferral in low/intermediate risk without other comorbidity; any CAC >0 → LDL-C goal <100 mg/dL, lower goals at higher scores.
CAC score — men ≥40 / women ≥45, PREVENT 3–<10%, when statin decision uncertain (Class 1)
PREVENT-ASCVD 10/30-yr risk, ages 30–79, every 4–6 yr

edits.match: Pending update — 2026 ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia Guideline supersedes the 2018 Cholesterol Guideline.
edits.new: **2026 ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia Guideline (published Mar 13, 2026; Circulation/JACC) replaces the 2018 Cholesterol Guideline.** Key changes: numeric LDL-C goals (<55 very-high-risk ASCVD / <70 high risk / <100 borderline-intermediate) with paired non-HDL-C goals (<100 / <130); one-time universal Lp(a); selective apoB; PREVENT-ASCVD (ages 30–79) replaces Pooled Cohort Equations with new strata (<3 / 3–<5 / 5–<10 / ≥10%); CAC upgraded to Class 1.

edits.match: USPSTF vs. ACC/AHA scope mismatch.
edits.new: **Risk-tool conflict (federal vs specialty).** USPSTF 2022 statin grades use Pooled Cohort Equations (Grade B ≥10%, Grade C 7.5–<10%, ages 40–75 with ≥1 risk factor); ACC/AHA 2026 uses PREVENT with intermediate risk 5–<10%. Thresholds are not interchangeable; federal precedence applies to coverage-linked preventive statin decisions — document which tool was used.
aao-hcq-2025

edits.match: hydroxychloroquine requires only baseline labs but mandates annual ophthalmologic screening with visual fields and SD-OCT starting at 5 years of use (sooner with risk factors), with the dose capped at ≤5 mg/kg actual body weight
edits.new: hydroxychloroquine requires only baseline labs; retinal screening (AAO 2025) is a baseline fundus + SD-OCT + wide-field fundus autofluorescence (FAF) soon after starting, then annual OCT + FAF while on HCQ (may be deferred during the first 5 years only if no significant risk factors), with dose ≤5.0 mg/kg real body weight/day (<400 mg/day in severe obesity)

edits.match: Dilated fundus + visual fields + SD-OCT — baseline within first year of HCQ use
edits.new: **HCQ retinal screening** — baseline fundus + SD-OCT + wide-field FAF soon after initiation; annual SD-OCT + FAF while on HCQ (may defer during years 1–5 if no risk factors: dose >5 mg/kg real weight, renal disease, tamoxifen, older age at initiation). Visual fields (e.g., 24-2C) and mfERG are secondary confirmatory tests; screen for both parafoveal and pericentral patterns.
HCQ: SD-OCT + FAF (baseline; annually — may defer yrs 1–5 if no risk factors)

edits.match: HCQ retinopathy screening. AAO recommends starting annual screening at year 5
edits.new: **HCQ retinopathy screening.** AAO 2025 revision: OCT + FAF are primary tools (VF/mfERG confirmatory); annual screening is the default and may be deferred during years 1–5 only without risk factors. Conservative synthesis: baseline + annual from start when any risk factor is present.

edits.match: Targets: ACR/EULAR Boolean remission (TJC ≤1, SJC ≤1, CRP ≤1 mg/dL, PtGA ≤1)
edits.new: Targets: ACR/EULAR Boolean 2.0 remission (TJC ≤1, SJC ≤1, CRP ≤1 mg/dL, PtGA ≤2 on 0–10 scale)

edits.match: EULAR 2019 and some real-world data
edits.new: EULAR (2019; RA management recommendations updated 2025) and some real-world data

edits.match: Vaccination review — annually (influenza, pneumococcal, recombinant zoster, COVID-19, Tdap).
edits.new: **Vaccination review** — annually (ACR 2022 + current CDC schedule): influenza annually; pneumococcal conjugate (PCV15/20/21) for all adults ≥50 and younger adults with risk conditions incl. immunosuppression; recombinant zoster; RSV (single dose ≥75; 50–74 if at increased risk); COVID-19 by individual-based (shared clinical) decision-making; Tdap/Td.
TB screening (if ongoing exposure risk); vaccination status review (influenza, pneumococcal, RZV, RSV, COVID-19 [shared decision])

edits.match: The 2019 ACR/AF guideline does not recommend routine surveillance imaging
edits.new: The 2019 ACR/AF guideline does not recommend routine surveillance imaging (not reversed by the 2026 ACR update, which strongly recommends ultrasound guidance for hip intra-articular glucocorticoid injection)

edits.match: CBC, creatinine / eGFR, blood pressure — periodically
edits.new: **Methotrexate for erosive hand OA (conditional; direction changed in 2026)** — apply RA methotrexate safety labs: CBC, ALT/AST, creatinine at baseline; every 2–4 weeks first 3 months; every 8–12 weeks months 3–6; every 12 weeks thereafter. Methotrexate is conditionally recommended against for knee/hip OA.

edits.match: BMI and weight — at each visit for overweight / obese hip and knee OA
edits.new: **BMI and weight** — each visit for overweight / obese hip and knee OA (weight loss strongly recommended); target ≥5% body-weight loss. GLP-1 RA conditionally recommended (new 2026) with diet and exercise in knee OA with obesity — monitor weight trajectory and GI tolerance.

edits.match: Acetaminophen for OA disagreement. ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends it
edits.new: **Acetaminophen for OA disagreement.** ACR 2026 update retains a conditional recommendation for acetaminophen (knee, hip, hand), with hepatotoxicity monitoring as before; NICE 2022 (UK) recommends against routine acetaminophen — an internationally relevant divergence.

edits.match: There is no major US guideline endorsing scheduled OA imaging surveillance, in contrast with common clinical practice.
edits.new: There is no major US guideline endorsing scheduled OA imaging surveillance, in contrast with common clinical practice; the ACR 2026 update (summary posted Sep 2026; full manuscript pending) does not address surveillance imaging.

edits.match: Mental-health screening (depression, anxiety, sleep, coping) — periodically.
edits.new: **Mental-health screening (depression, anxiety, sleep, coping)** — periodically. CBT conditionally recommended for knee, hip, and hand OA (ACR 2026).
aua-bph-2026

edits.match: Patients started on an alpha-blocker, PDE5 inhibitor, beta-3 agonist, or anticholinergic should be reassessed at 4–12 weeks (typically ≈4 weeks) for response and tolerability; those on a 5-ARI are reassessed at 3–6 months,
edits.new: After initiating treatment, patients should be re-evaluated within 6 months with standardized symptom scores and adverse-event review; without improvement, pursue an alternative diagnosis and/or treatment pathway. On a 5-ARI,

edits.match: Treatment-response reassessment — 4–12 weeks after starting medical therapy
edits.new: **Treatment-response reassessment** — within 6 months after initiating treatment: standardized symptom score (IPSS) + adverse events. Without improvement → pursue alternative diagnosis and/or treatment pathway.

edits.match: Post-procedural follow-up (TURP, PVP, HoLEP / ThuLEP
edits.new: **Post-procedural follow-up (TURP, PVP, HoLEP / ThuLEP, WVTT / Rezum, PUL / UroLift, PAE, TIPD)** — evaluate for at least 1 year to assess response (standardized symptom score + adverse events; PVR and uroflowmetry may be assessed).
IPSS annual reassessment (watchful waiting)

Post-void residual (PVR — retention; required pre-procedure; may be offered at follow-up); uroflowmetry (retention / exclude other disorders); response visit within 6 mo after initiating treatment; post-procedural follow-up for ≥1 yr

edits.match: No routine imaging is recommended for surveillance.
edits.new: **No routine surveillance imaging.** Before a procedural intervention, use imaging to assess the volume and shape of the prostate (Clinical Principle). Cystoscopy may be performed before a procedure (Clinical Principle), and may be offered with pressure-flow testing / UDS if LUTS worsen during follow-up (Expert Opinion).
Prostate volume / shape imaging before procedural intervention

edits.match: Post-void residual (PVR) — as indicated at baseline if obstruction or retention suspected
edits.new: **Post-void residual (PVR)** — may be obtained to evaluate for retention or exclude other disorders (Clinical Principle); may be offered during routine follow-up (Expert Opinion); required before a procedural intervention (Clinical Principle).

edits.match: PSA — offered at baseline when prostate-cancer diagnosis would change management
edits.new: **PSA** — may be obtained at the initial evaluation after shared decision-making (Expert Opinion). 5-ARI candidacy: prostate volume >30 cc and/or PSA >1.5 ng/mL; counsel on adverse effects and the impact on prostate-cancer diagnosis. Repeat per shared-decision PCa screening cadence (USPSTF: every 2–4 years for ages 55–69).

edits.match: (estimates prostate volume; cutoff >1.5 ng/mL guides 5-ARI candidacy)
edits.new: (estimates prostate volume; prostate volume >30 cc and/or PSA >1.5 ng/mL defines 5-ARI candidacy)

edits.match: PVR and uroflowmetry as routine surveillance. AUA lists both as conditional / optional
edits.new: **PVR and uroflowmetry as routine surveillance.** AUA 2026: may be obtained to evaluate for retention or exclude other disorders and may be offered during routine follow-up (Expert Opinion); PVR is required before a procedural intervention. AAFP 2023 notes PVR is not useful for routine monitoring. Conservative synthesis: not routine annually; obtain with worsening symptoms and pre-procedure.

edits.match: The gap is closed via shared decision-making.
edits.new: The gap is closed via shared decision-making. The USPSTF prostate-cancer screening topic is being updated (final research plan Dec 2023); the 2018 statement remains in force.
ada-soc-2026
aace-dm-2026

edits.match: Fasting lipid panel — at diagnosis and initial evaluation; every 5 years if <40
edits.new: **Lipid panel** — at diagnosis / initial evaluation, then annually if not on lipid-lowering therapy (Rec 10.16); at LLT initiation, 4–12 weeks after initiation or dose change, and annually thereafter (10.17). Targets: LDL <70 mg/dL primary prevention age 40–75 at higher risk; LDL <55 mg/dL with ASCVD (and ≥50% reduction).
UACR, Cr / eGFR (no CKD), lipid panel (all; on or off statin), ALT / AST + FIB-4 (MASLD screen), TSH (periodic)

edits.match: Serum potassium — at initiation, dose change, and periodically on ACEi
edits.new: **Serum K+ / eGFR** — at initiation and periodically on ACEi / ARB / steroidal MRA (Rec 10.11 / 11.6b); nonsteroidal MRA (finerenone; eGFR ≥25): K+ 1 month after initiation, then periodically (11.8); diuretics: hypokalemia check at routine visits and 7–14 days after initiation or dose change.
B12 (metformin >5 yr); K+ (ACEi/ARB/MRA at start + periodically; finerenone at 1 mo; diuretic 7–14 d after start/dose change); risk-tier CKD labs (G3 q6–12 mo, G4 q3–5 mo, G5 q1–3 mo)

edits.match: ALT / AST with FIB-4 (MASLD screen) — at diagnosis and annually
edits.new: **ALT / AST with FIB-4 (MASLD screen)** — at diagnosis and annually; FIB-4 <1.3 low risk; FIB-4 >2.67 → refer to liver specialist. Prefer a GLP-1 RA with MASH benefit when at high fibrosis risk.

edits.match: Vitamin B12 — periodically on long-term metformin
edits.new: **Vitamin B12** — periodically on metformin >5 years; sooner with anemia or neuropathy.

edits.match: DEXA bone density — ≥5 years post-diagnosis
edits.new: **DXA bone density** — every 2–3 years in adults ≥65 with diabetes and in younger adults with diabetes plus multiple fracture risk factors (Rec 4.9). In T2D interpret T-score ≤−2.0 as equivalent to −2.5; consider osteoporosis drug therapy at T-score ≤−2.5, or −2.0 to −2.5 with added fracture risk (4.13a/b). Avoid TZDs and sulfonylureas when fracture risk is high.
DXA q2–3 yr (≥65, or younger with multiple fracture risk factors)

edits.match: Blood pressure — every routine visit; home BP encouraged.
edits.new: **Blood pressure** — every routine visit, or at least every 6 months (Rec 10.1); counsel all with HTN on home BP monitoring (10.2). Target <130/80 if safely attainable; SBP <120 should be encouraged in high CV or kidney risk (10.4). Older adults: <130/80 if safe; <140/90 for poor health or limited life expectancy (13.9).

edits.match: Comprehensive foot exam (inspection, pulses, 10-g monofilament
edits.new: **PAD screen** — at initial evaluation: lower-extremity pulses, capillary refill, dependent rubor, elevation pallor, venous filling time. Refer for ABI with toe pressures if claudication, rest pain, or decreased / absent pedal pulses.

edits.match: Comprehensive foot exam (inspection, pulses, 10-g monofilament
edits.new: **Comprehensive foot exam (inspection, deformity, pulses; 10-g monofilament or Ipswich touch test + one of pinprick / temperature / vibration)** — at least annually; every visit if prior ulcer / amputation / sensory loss.

edits.match: CGM-derived Time in Range (TIR) — reviewed at each visit if patient uses CGM.
edits.new: **CGM** — recommended from diagnosis for people on insulin or noninsulin hypoglycemia-causing therapy (Rec 7.15); recommended for older adults with T2D on insulin (13.5); consider for T2D on basal insulin. Review at each visit: TIR >70% and TBR <70 mg/dL <4% for most adults; older adults with complex / intermediate health TIR ≥50% and TBR <1%; TBR <54 mg/dL <1%.

edits.match: Anxiety / fear of hypoglycemia (GAD-7) — at least annually.
edits.new: **Anxiety (GAD-7)** — at least annually (Rec 5.46). Fear of hypoglycemia — at least annually in high-risk or severe-hypoglycemia patients (5.47). If distress is not addressed at the visit, refer to behavioral health (5.45).

edits.match: Disordered eating screen — at least annually.
edits.new: **Sleep health screen** — routinely (new 2026 Rec 5.56).

edits.match: Vaccination review (influenza annually; pneumococcal; HBV if <60
edits.new: **Vaccination review** — annually per CDC schedule / ADA Table 4.3: influenza annually; pneumococcal conjugate (PCV15/20/21) all adults ≥50 and younger with risk conditions; HBV if <60 (≥60 at clinician discretion); RZV ≥50; Tdap/Td; RSV single dose ≥75 and 50–74 at increased risk; COVID-19 by individual-based (shared clinical) decision-making.
CGM review (if on CGM; CGM recommended if on insulin / hypoglycemia-causing agents)

edits.match: BP target. ADA 2025: <130/80 with consideration
edits.new: **BP target.** ADA 2026: <130/80 if safely attainable; SBP <120 should be encouraged in high CV / kidney risk (Rec 10.4). AHA/ACC 2025: <130/80 for all adults.

edits.match: A1c target disagreement. ADA: <7% for most nonpregnant adults
edits.new: **A1c target disagreement.** ADA: <7% for most nonpregnant adults; <6.5% may be appropriate with good health and low hypoglycemia risk (Rec 6.4). AACE: ≤6.5% when safely achievable (2023 figure; confirm in 2026 algorithm). AGS: 7.5–8% for most older adults, with explicit caution against <6.5% in this group.

edits.match: ADA aligns but allows simpler annual monitoring in stable patients with normal eGFR and UACR.
edits.new: ADA aligns but allows simpler annual monitoring in stable patients with normal eGFR and UACR. A KDIGO 2026 Diabetes-and-CKD focused-update draft (public review closed Apr 2026) is under revision; the 2022 guideline remains current.

edits.match: ASCVD 10-year risk estimation (PREVENT) — annually
edits.new: **10-yr ASCVD risk (PREVENT-ASCVD, ages 30–79)** — periodically, per the 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline (ADA co-issuing society); ADA 2026 Section 10 assigns statin intensity by age and risk factors without naming a calculator.

edits.match: Cardiovascular surveillance includes annual ASCVD risk estimation (PREVENT)
edits.new: Cardiovascular surveillance includes periodic ASCVD risk estimation (PREVENT)

edits.match: lipid panel (annually once on a statin)
edits.new: lipid panel (annually, on or off statin)
